---
title: "1) Copernicus account and credentials"
lang: en
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Start here
This page is the **heart of the repository**: it is where you get the credentials that
go into `.env`. Follow the steps in order and fill in each field.
:::

The **Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE)** offers **two kinds of authentication**,
used by different parts of the code:

| Type | What it is | Used for | Variables in `.env` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OAuth client** | `client_id` + `client_secret` | Statistical API (time series) | `CDSE_CLIENT_ID`, `CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET` |
| **Account login** | e-mail + password | OData (catalog and raw L2) | `CDSE_USERNAME`, `CDSE_PASSWORD` |

![Pipeline flow: account + `.env` feed the series and the maps](../img/fluxo.svg){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

## Step 1 — Create the account

1. Go to <https://dataspace.copernicus.eu> and click **Register**.
2. Fill in e-mail, password and details. **Confirm the activation e-mail** (check spam).
3. Log in at <https://dataspace.copernicus.eu>.

::: {.callout-warning}
Without confirming the e-mail, login will not complete — the most common cause of
`401`/`403` errors later.
:::

## Step 2 — Create the OAuth client (for time series)

1. Open the settings dashboard:
   <https://shapps.dataspace.copernicus.eu/dashboard/#/account/settings>
   (log in with the same account).
2. In the side menu, go to **User settings → OAuth clients**.
3. Click **Create**.
4. Give it a name (e.g. `tropomi-ch4`) and choose the expiry. Recommended:
   **Never expire**.
5. Click **Create** again. The panel shows the **client_id** and **client_secret**.

::: {.callout-important}
The **client_secret is shown only once**. Copy and store it now. If you lose it,
delete the client and create a new one.
:::

```bash
CDSE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

## Step 3 — Account login (for raw L2)

Downloading the **raw L2** (1 km maps) uses the **normal login**, not the OAuth client.
Use the **same e-mail and password** as the account:

```bash
CDSE_USERNAME=you@example.com
CDSE_PASSWORD=your-password
```

Under the hood, the code authenticates with `grant_type=password` and
`client_id=cdse-public` (the CDSE public client, not yours).

## Step 4 — Google Earth Engine (optional)

Only needed for GEE maps (page 7):

1. Go to <https://code.earthengine.google.com/> and sign in with Google.
2. Accept the terms and **register a Cloud Project**.
3. Copy the **Project ID**.

```bash
GEE_PROJECT=your-project-id
GEE_DRIVE_FOLDER=CH4_TROPOMI_Brasil
```

## Summary: where to get each variable

| Variable in `.env` | What it is | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `CDSE_CLIENT_ID` | OAuth client ID | Dashboard → *User settings → OAuth clients* |
| `CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET` | OAuth client secret | same (shown **once**) |
| `CDSE_USERNAME` | Account e-mail | the one you registered at CDSE |
| `CDSE_PASSWORD` | Account password | the one you registered at CDSE |
| `GEE_PROJECT` | Earth Engine project ID | <https://code.earthengine.google.com/> |
| `CDSE_*_URL` | API endpoints | page [API links](02-links-api.qmd) |

## Common issues

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401` at login | e-mail not confirmed | confirm the e-mail and retry |
| `401`/`403` on series | wrong `client_id`/`secret` | re-copy or recreate the OAuth client |
| `client_secret` lost | shown only once | delete the client and create a new one |
| `404` on L2 | wrong product ID/endpoint | check the [API links](02-links-api.qmd) page |
